decision: set the definition of done as a falsifiable predicate covering the published url, the loud failure, and the idempotent second run
why: the whole point of this product is that both prior attempts never published anything, so the finish line has to be a url and a second run that does nothing

decision: set rigor high on the publish spine and medium on the curator logic
why: the spine is a one-way door that is cheap to settle now and expensive to settle later, and the curator is fully reversible

decision: found that harness.root ignores its agent option when the root already exists
why: the existing src/harness.ts looked like it applied the model on every run and does not, so a provider change would silently never take effect

decision: found that pi-durable has no public way to enumerate a document family
why: any design that needs to list seen articles has to own a key index, which pushed the seen-set decision

decision: found that the designed publish chain had no build step and mixed two branches
why: the publisher wrote content on master while Pages served main, and nothing rebuilt dist, so a successful publish would have left the site stale

decision: picked candidate A as the base and candidate B as the donor
why: A had the coherent attempt and failure state, the correct request-identifier resume, and the only credible seen-set

decision: grafted B's reference-only answer shape and angle-bracket link destinations onto A
why: A asked the model for a summary and a reason and rendered links as (url), which a feed-controlled url can break out of

decision: rejected B's absence of an article-level seen-set
why: B dissolves the question, which leaves a story that appears on two feeds on two days published twice
evidence: openspec/changes/add-slopchop-newsletter/design.md, The seen-set belongs to the published artifact

decision: reproduced that a javascript link survives contentlayer's markdown pipeline unchanged
why: the earlier measurement that raw html is dropped had been read as safety, and it says nothing about link schemes

decision: reproduced that a url containing a closing parenthesis is truncated when written as a markdown destination
why: this is a content-integrity bug on a page under the author's name, not a theoretical one

decision: resolved the quiet-day question by stating a default instead of leaving it open
why: the task instruction says an open question that changes what gets built has to be resolved first, and the change is one branch in the renderer if the owner wants the other behaviour

decision: sequenced the artifact first and the curator second
why: both prior attempts built a pipeline and never shipped a page, so the page has to exist before the pipeline is worth building

decision: moved the arena artifacts into the repository so the trail's evidence resolves after the run
why: two rows pointed at /tmp paths that will not survive, and the audit checks that every evidence pointer resolves

decision: recorded the design's provenance: the two arena candidates and the grounding they were given
why: a reviewer deciding whether the synthesis was right needs the candidates, not only the conclusion

decision: tightened the git tree claim after checking it against a live repository
why: the design said the tree api has no such cap, and it has a much larger ceiling and a truncation flag, which changes what the publisher must check

decision: split the model work into a cheap selection call and an expensive composition call
why: one call would carry all thirty bodies, about 45k input tokens against 20k for the split, and would ask one model to rank and write in the same answer

decision: made the model answer with references into a candidate table instead of with urls
why: a reference the app offered is the only thing that can become a link, so the model has no way to author a url at all

decision: gave each attempt its own conversation and stored its id in the date record
why: a day's model context must not contain another day's bodies or a previous failed attempt, and the request id is idempotent per conversation
evidence: openspec/changes/add-slopchop-newsletter/design.md, A day is its own conversation

decision: made the request identifier carry the date, the attempt number and the stage
why: the attempt number is the one thing that separates a crash from a wrong answer, so a crash resumes free and a failure is paid for again
evidence: openspec/changes/add-slopchop-newsletter/design.md, The request id carries the attempt

decision: decided the article bodies are never stored
why: they are the cheapest thing to recompute at about thirty-six seconds, while the model's choice and prose are what a retry cannot afford to recompute

decision: bounded both the dates and the seen-set with one coverage window of three days
why: the feeds carry a rolling window of recent items, and a url covered more than three days ago is old news

decision: put an exclusive lock over the whole run
why: the github branch is a genuine single write target and one process owns a storage at a time, so serialising is the right answer here

decision: resolved the quiet-day question with a stated default
why: the task instruction says an open question that changes what gets built has to be resolved first, and the change is one branch in the renderer if the owner wants the other behaviour

decision: ran openspec validate on the change and it passed strict
why: a change that does not validate is not a change, and the result was not recorded anywhere

decision: ran an audit of this trail and applied every finding it raised
why: an adversarial read of the trail found a mispointed evidence row, a task that asserted the opposite of the measured behaviour, a predicate that contradicted the spec, and a missing task for the provider reconfiguration bug

decision: committed the contentlayer reproduction so the two safety holes are diffable rather than asserted
why: the trail claimed a reproduction that only existed in a temp directory, and the audit checks that every evidence pointer resolves

decision: added the missing task for the provider reconfiguration bug
why: the trail proved that an existing root ignores a new agent, but no task said to change it, so a green provider spike could have hidden a production run still on the old provider

decision: supersedes the row that pointed the javascript reproduction at a temp path
why: that path held the parenthesis probe rather than the scheme probe, so the row did not show what it claimed

decision: supersedes the row that said two evidence pointers were ephemeral
why: three of them still pointed at temp paths, so the count was wrong

decision: supersedes the plan row that recorded the broken publish chain
why: the design states the corrected architecture rather than the earlier broken branch and build chain, so the row now points at the correction
evidence: openspec/changes/add-slopchop-newsletter/design.md, The site is one branch, one workflow, and one encoding

decision: supersedes the row that said a story on two feeds on two days would be published twice
why: the mechanism deduplicates canonical urls, not stories, and that is what the seen-set does
evidence: openspec/changes/add-slopchop-newsletter/design.md, The seen-set belongs to the published artifact
